topic: The Amazon is not the lungs of the Earth
lesson: The Amazon uses up almost exactly as much oxygen as it makes, so its net oxygen contribution is near zero, and its real importance is as a carbon store, a rainfall engine and a biodiversity vault.

post.caption:
Decomposition and respiration inside the Amazon consume nearly all the oxygen its photosynthesis produces, so the net contribution is close to zero. Ocean phytoplankton produce far more of what we breathe. That does not make the Amazon unimportant. It is a huge carbon store, a rainfall engine and a biodiversity vault.
